# listmonk_template (Resource)

Manages a listmonk e-mail template. Use `listmonk_default_template` to make a campaign template the default.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Campaign templates must render the campaign body with {{ template "content" . }}.
resource "listmonk_template" "branded" {
  name = "Branded"
  type = "campaign"
  body = file("${path.module}/templates/branded.html")
}

# Transactional templates have a fixed subject and are sent with POST /api/tx.
resource "listmonk_template" "welcome" {
  name    = "Welcome"
  type    = "tx"
  subject = "Welcome, {{ .Subscriber.Name }}"
  body    = <<-HTML
    <p>Hi {{ .Subscriber.Name }},</p>
    <p>Thanks for signing up.</p>
  HTML
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `body` (String) Template body (Go `html/template`). Campaign templates must contain `{{ template "content" . }}`.
- `name` (String) Name of the template.
- `type` (String) `campaign`, `campaign_visual` or `tx` (transactional). Changing it replaces the template.

### Optional

- `body_source` (String) Source document of the visual editor, for `campaign_visual` templates. listmonk cannot clear it once set, so removing this argument keeps the current value.
- `subject` (String) Subject line. Required for `tx` templates and not allowed for campaign templates (a campaign sets its own subject).

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Numeric ID of the template.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the default campaign template.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Templates are imported by their numeric ID.
terraform import listmonk_template.branded 5
```
